sections.name: architecture
sections.value: Doctrine: .agents-skills-port/pij-team/TENETS.md (tenets 1-6). This repo: Rust crates are the boundaries (crates/core types · crates/store adapter · crates/daemon http/composition root; arch-allowlist checked by `harness checks`); the pi extension lives in .pi/extensions/pij with core/ pi-free and fakes-tested (session.ts), adapters/ holding the runtime seams (rust-runtime.ts, daemon-http.ts). THE ONE FACT THIS PLAN MOVES: who knows a boot is fresh. Today the extension infers it from 'no row exists' (true under legacy, false under rs). After: the daemon states it. Vocabulary (frozen): `binding` = `created` (no row existed) | `rebound` (row existed, proc.pid/proc_start differ from stored) | `same` (row existed, same proc). fresh := binding !== 'same'. Extras-first: `binding` is an added optional field on the register response; nothing renamed. Seams: (1) crates/store registry put → must surface inserted-vs-updated + previous proc (pre-read inside the same transaction, or RETURNING with a CASE); (2) crates/daemon http register → sets binding; (3) core/daemon-wire.ts RustSeatDescriptor.binding?; (4) rust-runtime.ts boot passes `fresh` into session.boot; (5) core/session.ts BootInput.fresh?: boolean, `fresh = input.fresh ?? (liveDescriptor===null || wasDissolved)`. Golden fixture assets/contracts/register-response.json is the shared artifact both suites assert against (cross-runtime literal seam rule).

value.rationale: Two units in two runtimes behind one frozen field; they share no file. u0 (fixture + vocabulary) is PM-owned wave 0. Compose = one PM wiring pass + live proof; nothing to negotiate at compose time if the fixture is honoured.

value.name: contract fixture
value.responsibility: Three canonical register responses (created/rebound/same) as JSON, plus the vocabulary note.
value.interface: register-response.json: {"created": {...RustSeatDescriptor, "binding":"created"}, "rebound": {...,"binding":"rebound"}, "same": {...,"binding":"same"}} — descriptor fields exactly as /v1/register returns today plus binding.
value.test_strategy: Consumed by u1 and u2 tests; no tests of its own.
value.note: PM writes it before spawning anyone (tenet 2).

value.name: rs register binding
value.paths: crates/store/src/registry.rs, crates/store/tests/**, crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs (register handler + response type only), crates/daemon/src/http/tests.rs, crates/core/src/wire.rs (additive field only)
value.responsibility: Make the daemon report binding on /v1/register.
value.interface: Registry trait gains `async fn put_reporting(&self, d: SeatDescriptor) -> Result<(Seq, PutBinding)>` where `PutBinding { inserted: bool, previous_proc: Option<ProcIdentity> }` (existing `put` keeps its signature and delegates); handler computes binding = inserted ? created : (previous_proc != request.proc ? rebound : same) and serializes `"binding":"created"|"rebound"|"same"` on the response. Field is `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = Option::is_none)]` on the wire type.
value.test_strategy: `cargo test -p pij-store -p pij-daemon`: store test for each of the three outcomes on the sqlite fake/temp db; http test that serializes each response and byte-compares against the golden fixture entries (read from the fixture path, not restated). RED first.
value.note: No spine kind changes; seat.put stays. Do not touch delivery/**.

value.name: extension fresh-from-binding
value.responsibility: Derive fresh from the daemon's binding and prove the announce fires on rs boots.
value.interface: RustSeatDescriptor.binding?: 'created'|'rebound'|'same'; BootInput.fresh?: boolean; RustRuntimeSession.boot: `this.session.boot({...input, id: acceptedId, fresh: accepted.binding === undefined ? undefined : accepted.binding !== 'same'})` — undefined preserves today's inference for an old daemon.
value.test_strategy: rust-runtime.test.ts: fake client returns each fixture entry (parsed from the golden file); assert pi.inject called once with announceText for created and rebound, zero times for same; assert reload with `same` never announces. Run the new test on the pre-fix tree first and paste the RED. `bun test .pi/extensions/pij` green; core/session.test.ts must show no diff.
value.note: Sibling hazard: none — u1 is Rust-only. Legacy PijSession path unchanged apart from the optional override.

Each coder branches off 135-rs-boot-announce into ../fs3-rs-boot-announce-<unit>; PM merges u1 then u2 (order irrelevant, no shared files). Toolchain pinned: rust per rust-toolchain, bun per repo — no unit may change either. The live daemon on this machine runs from a built binary: nobody restarts it except the PM at compose time.

value.steps: 1) Merge u1, run cargo gates. 2) Merge u2, run bun test + harness checks. 3) Commit; `just bounce-rs`-style rebuild+restart of the rs daemon (verify pid change + ping + env PIJ_TELEGRAM_ENV still set — a bare restart drops Telegram). 4) Live proof: control on main first is already recorded in assets/inputs; now spawn omp, capture announce from session jsonl + pane; then AC2 (reused id, new process) and AC3 (/new + /reload). 5) Record everything in assets/live-proof.md with commands and outputs.
value.integration_proof: On the rebuilt+restarted rs daemon: (1) `pij-rs spawn --harness omp --bin omp` → the seat's session jsonl contains exactly one `You are pij session <id>` user turn and the spine shows register→announce ordering; (2) hand-start omp in a pane holding an existing seat row → register response binding=rebound and one announce; (3) `/new` then `/reload` on that seat → binding=same on reload, no second announce for the same pi session id. All three transcripts + `pij-rs ping` pid evidence pasted in assets/live-proof.md.

value.inputs: plan.dd.md + this guide + branch diff; priority: the fresh derivation (is `same` ever wrong for a genuinely new process?), the fixture being READ not restated on both sides, RED evidence for AC5, legacy path untouched

value.text: rebound detection needs the PREVIOUS proc; a put that only returns changes() cannot tell rebound from same — retire by pre-reading the row inside the same write transaction (persist-before-mutate holds).
Old daemon + new extension: binding absent → undefined → today's inference. Covered by u2's undefined branch test.

Spawn pre-mints the row, so a spawned seat's extension register is always `rebound`/`same`, never `created` — fresh must be true for rebound (proc differs from the spawner's placeholder) — assert this specific case in u1 (placeholder proc vs real proc) and in the live AC1.
Daemon not restarted after the Rust change → fix invisible, greens honest. Compose step 3 is mandatory and its pid/ping output is part of done.
